items.specializes_in: Specializes in Foil, Epee, and Saber
items.overview:
Founded by passionate coaches and parents, Bay Area Fencing Club reflects a deep love for the Olympic sport through its top-notch facilities and world-class coaching staff, each with impeccable athletic achievements and coaching results. Committed to the growth and development of youth through fencing, the club emphasizes fostering excellence in athletes both on and off the fencing strips, supporting them academically, socially, and athletically. By instilling values of integrity, sportsmanship, and resilience, we strive for excellence individually and as a team. 

Since its founding in 2021, Bay Area Fencing Club has become one of the fastest-growing and largest clubs in the country, boasting two locations totaling over 24,000 square feet with 35 fencing strips. In addition to our professional sports facilities, we provide free WiFi and quiet study rooms for our students to attend online classes and complete homework before or after training. While our facilities are impressive, our most valuable assets are our distinguished coaches. Executive Coach Lisa served as the head coach at Stanford University for over 25 years. Coach Sergei, a World Cup champion and former Russian National Team coach, also led the Jordan National Team. Coach Vakhob, former head coach of the Uzbekistan National Team and an FIE referee, has won multiple international titles. Coach Sandro, a Maestro di Scherma level III (the highest coaching level in Italy), has produced three world champions and numerous top-level players, including a current Italian National Team member. Youth Director Coach Nate had a successful NCAA athletic career as the team captain of Drew University varsity fencing team.
Bay Area Fencing Club takes pride in being an active member of the communities it serves. We organized the "Fence for Peace" charitable tournament, raising over $5,000 for war victims in Ukraine. Our fencers also founded the Point Impact Foundation, a nonprofit organization dedicated to raising funds to help underprivileged children learn fencing. Additionally, we have sponsored the Saratoga Education Foundation and the Saratoga High School Journalism Club.

Beginner Classes: Introducing the fundamentals of fencing in a fun and engaging way.

Advanced and Elite Training: Intensive training for competitive fencers aiming to excel at national and international levels.

Community and Values

Join Us

The mission of the Peter Westbrook Foundation is to empower youth from underserved communities through academic enrichment, mentorship, and disciplined athletic engagement, preparing them for success in school, college, and life.

The Peter Westbrook Foundation (PWF) is a New York City–based nonprofit founded in 1991 by Peter Westbrook, the first African American to win an Olympic medal in fencing. Raised in poverty by a single mother in Newark, New Jersey, Peter discovered fencing through a community program that changed the trajectory of his life. That experience shaped his vision: to ensure that young people from under-resourced communities would have access not only to athletic opportunity, but to academic excellence and mentorship.

For more than three decades, PWF has served youth across all five boroughs of New York City, the majority of whom are Black or Latino/a and from low-income households. What began as a small program in a rented gym has grown into a nationally respected youth development organization that has produced not only Olympians and national champions, but more importantly, college graduates and young professionals.

items.name: South Youth Fencing Alliance (SYFA)
items.overview:
Areas of Focus:

South Youth Fencing Alliance (SYFA) specializes in Foil fencing for youth and adults.

New to fencing? Start here. Try fencing with us for a full week before deciding whether to join. We provide loaner equipment, so there is no need to buy gear just to see if fencing is right for you. Affordable monthly memberships and multiple weekly practices make it easy to get started.

SYFA is Southeast Minnesota’s premier fencing club and the region’s only dedicated brick-and-mortar fencing facility. Our fencers have a home for fencing, with coaches who know them, teammates they see regularly, and a place to train, play, compete, and belong.

We use fencing to help young people build work ethic, set goals, manage emotions under pressure, become better teammates, and develop a healthy competitive spirit. Our goal is to develop good humans. Becoming a great fencer along the way is a bonus.

The results have followed. SYFA athletes have earned three Minnesota State Championship titles in foil, Regional Championships and podium finishes, qualified for Junior Olympics and Summer Nationals, competed nationally, become NCAA fencers, and earned Academic All-American recognition.

We’re proud of the medals, titles, and qualifications, but they aren’t what defines success at SYFA. The growth behind them does.

Our schedule makes fencing work for busy families. We offer fencing five days a week, dedicated adult fencing, Saturday open fencing and team-building game days, private lessons, and occasional extra practices before major events. Miss one evening and you do not have to wait another week to fence.

Competition is encouraged, but it is always a choice. Some fencers love tournaments. Others simply love practicing, learning, playing games, and being with their teammates. You do not have to compete to be an important part of SYFA.

For those who do compete, SYFA travels together to selected local, regional, and national USA Fencing events. Athletes have coaches and teammates beside them from their first tournament through major championship events.

Whether you want to try fencing for the first time, fence recreationally, return to the sport as an adult, or pursue serious competitive goals, there is a place for you here.

Built For More.

items.name: Zeta Fencing
items.overview:
Founded in 2001 by 3-time Olympic National Team Coach Zoran Tulum, Zeta Fencing has become the leading sabre club in New England over its 20+ year history. During this time, the program has produced 3 Olympians, 4 NCAA champions, 5 world championship medalists, 36 world championship team qualifications, and countless national champions and medalists.

Regardless of the level of competitive commitment, the sport of fencing develops quick thinking, poise, agility and speed, as well as self-confidence and sportsmanship. Fencing is a lifetime sport, equally suitable for men and women, children and adults. Zeta Fencing offers classes at all levels, from beginner to elite, and all ages, from age 7 to adult.

In 2025, Zeta alumni, 3-time USA Olympian, and world champion Eli Dershwitz purchased and took over at his childhood club. He is dedicated to creating a top of the nation training environment at Zeta.
